preconditions: An existing closed day with nonempty saved financial reconciliation is required.
A legitimate active session without all/reports_view is required; no anonymous or login bypass claim.
Ordinary screen reachability may have additional navigation gates outside this bounded review; direct endpoint source path is sufficient to identify missing report gate, not proof every role sees UI.

Live report helper and client live guard correctly restrict the corresponding live report.
No HTTP/SQL/session or rendered UI experiment was performed.
contracts.impact: Authenticated actor lacking report permission can receive financial report JSON from snapshot endpoints under the inspected source contract. Different from employee report or identity-binding issues; parent owns dedup/security disposition.

evidence: Close54-59 reads/validates day state before transaction64; no in-transaction day refresh shown.
Close91 computes Count+1,92-93 demotes currently visible snapshots,95-108 stages new Authoritative snapshot and day pointer/revision; SaveChanges118.
DbContext400-405 declares PK Id, nonunique day index and Restrict FK; no unique day/revision or single-Authoritative index in inspected block.
Query44-46 chooses greatest revision among Authoritative with no tie-break.
contracts.proposed_schedule: Distinct close request IDs both validate same open/reopened day and execute count/demotion before either new snapshot is visible. Both may compute same revision and stage Authoritative=true. Whether both commits can succeed depends on actual EF command order, SQL locking and FK parent-lock interactions; not established by static inspection.
counterevidence: Same-request deterministic snapshot PK prevents duplicate persisted ID.
Existing parent/day FK and day update can serialize/block or yield conversion deadlock depending actual generated DML order; do not assume both succeed without provider proof.
If second count/demotion occurs after first commit, count advances and prior snapshot is demoted, defeating proposed duplicate-current outcome.
A single close transaction preserves its own atomic writes but is not itself proof of global admission serialization.
next_tests: Use controlled SQL Server barrier around count/demotion for two distinct close IDs, record actual EF DML order/locks and outcomes; no live production DB.
Assert one authoritative row, unique revisions and day pointer coherent after both success/failure scenarios, including existing snapshot history.
contracts.impact: Source lacks explicit common day admission lock/state token and schema uniqueness for archival invariants; duplicate-current/same-revision outcome remains a qualified provider-dependent candidate, not reproduced corruption.
